confirmed.title: Negative Content-Length bypasses the 15MB upload cap and reads unbounded data into memory
confirmed.claim: do_POST trusts the client's Content-Length without validating it is a non-negative integer, so a negative value defeats MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES and makes the server buffer the socket until EOF, and a non-numeric value crashes outside the error handler.
confirmed.evidence: Line 1107: `content_length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0) or 0)` runs BEFORE the try block; `Content-Length: abc` raises an uncaught ValueError (connection dropped, no JSON error response). A negative value (e.g. `Content-Length: -1`) passes the `content_length > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` check (negative is not greater), then line 1137 `body = self.rfile.read(content_length)` — BufferedReader.read with a negative size reads until EOF, so a client on this public demo API can stream gigabytes into RAM on one connection, exactly the DoS the 15MB cap exists to prevent. Fix is one guard: parse in the try block and reject anything not 0 < n <= MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES.
confirmed.verdict_note:
Traced the real path in C:/FYP/web/server.py and could not refute it.

Code as written (lines 1102-1144):
- 1107 `content_length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0) or 0)` sits BEFORE the `try:` at 1112. `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` never parses or validates Content-Length itself (it never touches the body), so a header value of `abc` reaches `int()` and raises an uncaught ValueError. `handle_one_request` only catches `socket.timeout`, so it propagates to `socketserver.handle_error`: traceback to stderr, connection dropped, no JSON body, no status line. Confirmed: the two ValueError/Exception handlers at 1121/1123 cannot see it because they are scoped to the `try` that starts five lines later.
- 1108 `if content_length > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is the only pre-read cap, and `-1 > 15728640` is False, so a negative value passes.
- 1113 -> 1137 `body = self.rfile.read(content_length)`. `rfile` is `socket.makefile('rb')` -> BufferedReader; `read(negative)` reads until EOF. Verified empirically with a socketpair: `rfile.read(-1)` returned the full 500 KB the peer streamed before closing, i.e. it is size-unbounded, not a no-op or error.
- Both post-hoc size checks are downstream of the read: `len(image_bytes) > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` at 1116 runs after the whole body is in RAM, and `BytesParser.parsebytes` at 1138 makes another copy of it first. `read_multipart_image` checks Content-Type before reading (1134-1136), but the attacker controls that header too, so `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=x` + `Content-Length: -1` walks straight through.
- No mitigation elsewhere: no `timeout` attribute is set on the handler or server (grep found none), the server is a plain `ThreadingHTTPServer` (line 1169), and `scripts/deploy_hf_space.py:148` ships exactly this file as the container entrypoint (`CMD ["python","web/server.py","--host","0.0.0.0","--port","7860"]`), so it is the real serving path, not dev-only scaffolding. Nothing in the dated audit comments (85, 87-104) documents the cap's semantics as intentional; `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is a bare constant.

Why I downgraded high -> medium rather than confirming high:
- Impact is resource exhaustion on a single free-tier demo Space (worst case: OOM kill / restart of one container). No data exposure, no auth bypass, no corruption, and the process itself survives per-connection failures because each request runs on its own thread.
- A negative Content-Length is not a syntactically valid field per RFC 9110 (digits only), so the HF Spaces ingress in front of the container is likely to reject or normalize it; direct exploitation is most reliable against a locally run instance (default `--host 127.0.0.1`).
- The 15 MB cap is already porous in a way this finding does not depend on: with no socket timeout anywhere, a client can send a legal `Content-Length: 15728640` and trickle bytes, holding a thread open indefinitely. So the negative-length hole widens an already-soft limit rather than being the only thing standing between the server and exhaustion.
- Fix is genuinely one guard, as the finding says: move the parse inside the `try` and reject anything that is not `0 < n <= MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (a bare `except ValueError` there also turns the `Content-Length: abc` case into a clean 400 instead of a dropped connection).

confirmed.title: LBP feature does not implement its documented '10 uniform bins': 48 of 58 uniform patterns are silently dropped and bin 9 is a collision bucket
confirmed.claim: compute_lbp assigns the 58 uniform P=8 patterns sequential labels 0..57, maps all non-uniform patterns to 9, then histograms with bins=10 range=(0,10) — so pixels with uniform labels 10..57 are excluded from the histogram entirely, bin 9 conflates the 10th uniform pattern (value 14) with all 198 non-uniform patterns, and the result matches neither standard u2 (59-bin) nor riu2 (10-bin rotation-invariant) LBP that the docstring's '10 uniform bins' implies.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 101-105: `for label, val in enumerate(uniform_vals): lut[val] = label` gives labels 0..57 (58 uniform patterns for P=8, not 10); non-uniform -> 9, colliding with uniform_vals[9]. Line 108: `np.histogram(lbp_mapped, bins=10, range=(0, 10))` drops values >= 10, so a majority of uniform-pattern pixels (e.g. all-dark 255, edges like 0b00011100) contribute nothing, and normalization at line 109 divides by only the surviving pixels — the 10 features are a distorted sub-histogram, not the documented uniform-LBP descriptor. The correct 10-bin scheme (riu2) buckets uniform patterns by bit-count (9 classes) + 1 non-uniform class. IMPORTANT caveat: the same code produced the training features for best_convnext_ensemble_tuned.pth, so it is train-serve CONSISTENT — do not fix in isolation or the checkpoint's input distribution shifts; it needs a retrain, or correct the docstring/report text claiming 10 uniform bins. Related cosmetic note: compute_color_features labels BGR-order channel histograms as 'RGB' (lines 46-52).

confirmed.verdict_note: Confirmed by executing the LUT+histogram logic standalone. compute_lbp (scripts/custom_feature_extractor.py:90-110) assigns the 58 uniform P=8 patterns sequential labels 0..57, maps non-uniform to 9, then histograms with bins=10 range=(0,10). Verified: labels 11..57 are silently dropped (one off-by-one in the finding's evidence: np.histogram's inclusive right edge puts label 10, uniform pattern 15, into bin 9 — so 47 patterns are dropped, not 48, and bin 9 conflates uniform patterns 14 AND 15 with all 198 non-uniform patterns). Concrete wrong behavior: a flat crop yields LBP=255 everywhere (label 57) producing an ALL-ZERO histogram; a horizontal-gradient crop also yields all zeros; a random crop drops ~37% of pixels and line 109 normalizes over survivors only. This matches neither u2 (59-bin) nor riu2 (10-bin by bit-count) LBP; the docstring's 'maps 256 patterns to 10 uniform bins' describes riu2, which this is not. Refutation attempts failed: no dated comment or runs/audits sweep documents this as a measured decision (grep found zero LBP hits in runs/audits), and the module is live — web/server.py:222 and all training scripts import this exact extract_637_features (not the archive copy). Severity medium is appropriate: 10/637 features are a degraded, sometimes fully degenerate descriptor and the paper's methodology description is inaccurate, but there is no train-serve skew, crash, or prediction inconsistency.

Harmless output-wise, but it wastes a ConvNeXt+637-feature forward pass per small unsure box and means the documented banana-peel-style rescue silently excludes the 24-28 px range. Cheaper fallback: skip the retry entry entirely when the shrunk view is under the floor.
confirmed.verdict_note: Verified in web/server.py: size filter admits boxes >= 24 px per side (line 661); UNSURE_ZOOM_SHRINK=0.22 (line 120) makes the shrunk view 0.56x the raw box side (lines 726-729); when that is under the 16 px floor, line 732 falls back to r["crop"] — the exact padded-crop array already classified into verified_probs[i]. classify_bgr_tuned_batch (lines 542-571) is deterministic eval-mode inference, so the retry reproduces the original probs and the Background comparison at line 739 can never change the result. No dated comment documents this fallback as a measured decision; it exists only for retry_idx/zoom_crops index alignment. Minor precision fix: due to int(round(...)) the guaranteed-no-op range is min-side < ~26.8 px (not 28.57), with fallback still possible up to ~30 px depending on fractional coords, and it triggers off the smaller side of the box independently — slightly widening the affected population. Output is never wrong; cost is one wasted ConvNeXt forward + 637-feature extraction per small unsure box, and the zoom rescue silently never applies to the smallest boxes. Real, severity low is correct; fix is to skip the batch entry when the shrunk view is under the floor.

confirmed.title: HEAD requests bypass both /api/health handling and the API_ONLY branch
confirmed.claim: Only do_GET is overridden; do_HEAD is inherited from SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, so on the API-only HF Space a HEAD /api/health returns 404 (no web/api/health file) and HEAD / falls through to filesystem serving instead of the service card.
confirmed.evidence: Class WasteWiseHandler overrides do_GET (line 1067) and do_POST but not do_HEAD, which BaseHTTPRequestHandler dispatches to SimpleHTTPRequestHandler.send_head against WEB_DIR. Scenario: an uptime monitor configured with HEAD https://<space>.hf.space/api/health (HEAD is the default for several monitors) gets 404 and flags the healthy service as down. Fix: `do_HEAD = do_GET`-style handling or route HEAD for /api/* through the same JSON logic (headers-only).
confirmed.verdict_note: Confirmed by reading web/server.py: WasteWiseHandler overrides do_OPTIONS/do_GET/do_POST but not do_HEAD, so HEAD requests fall through to SimpleHTTPRequestHandler.send_head resolved against WEB_DIR. HEAD /api/health looks for a file web/api/health, which does not exist, and returns 404 while GET returns 200 JSON — an RFC 9110 violation (HEAD must mirror GET). On the HF Space deploy (scripts/deploy_hf_space.py copies only server.py into web/), HEAD / also bypasses the API_ONLY service-card branch at line 1089 and serves a filesystem directory listing. No do_HEAD, no deploy-side mitigation, and no dated comment marking this as a measured decision. Impact is limited to HEAD-based uptime monitors falsely reporting the service down; nothing functional breaks for the frontend (which uses GET/POST), so severity low is correct.

confirmed.title: Dedup survivor selection includes Background prob, so a Background-decisive duplicate can erase a material detection
confirmed.claim: Dedup ranks duplicate boxes by `np.max(verified_probs[i])` over all 7 classes including Background, so for a near-duplicate pair classified (Background 0.95) vs (plastic 0.75), the Background view survives and the material view is discarded — removing the object from material votes, detections, and the mixed-load hint, contradicting the adjacent zoom-retry rationale that avoids letting the emptier view's Background veto real objects.
confirmed.evidence: Line 757-761: `order = sorted(range(verified_crop_count), key=lambda i: float(np.max(verified_probs[i])), reverse=True)` — the comment (line 746) says the survivor should be 'the most decisive view', but decisiveness-about-Background wins against decisiveness-about-a-material. After dedup the kept Background box contributes nothing to material_counts (line 900-902 skips Background) and the object disappears from the headline vote. Ranking by `np.max(verified_probs[i][:6])` (material decisiveness) would keep current behavior for material/material pairs and fix the Background veto; worth a measured check against the fusion sweep before changing.
confirmed.verdict_note: Confirmed by tracing web/server.py. Dedup ranking (line 757-761) uses np.max over all 7 classes including Background (index 6), so for a duplicate pair (IoU>0.55) classified Background 0.95 vs plastic 0.75, the Background view survives, fuses to Background (bg_prob dominates line 874-875), and is skipped from material votes at line 900-902 — the object vanishes from material_counts, weights, and the mixed-load hint. Neither box triggers the UNSURE_ZOOM retry (both maxes >= 0.55 conf threshold), so nothing rescues it. Refutation attempts failed: (a) the sweep runs/audits/box_dedup_dense_retry_sweep_2026-07-27.json measured dedup on/off and image sizes but never the ranking criterion, so max-over-7 is not a measured decision — and its A_test data even shows plastic->background confusions rising 1->2 when dedup was enabled; (b) the adjacent zoom-retry comment (lines 736-740) documents the opposite policy ("averaging lets the emptier view's Background veto real objects"), so project intent contradicts the dedup ranking; (c) deploy_hf_space.py sets no WASTEWISE_ overrides, so the default IoU 0.55 ships and duplicate boxes are the norm (NMS-free YOLO26 is the reason dedup exists). Severity low is correct: at most one material vote lost per duplicate pair, and the counter-hypothesis (a decisive Background call correctly suppressing a false-positive box) is plausible enough that the [:6] fix should be sweep-validated before changing, as the finding itself notes.

confirmed.title: yoloIou reported as active config though the server's own comment documents iou= is ignored; live fusion knobs absent from health
confirmed.claim: YOLO_IOU=0.55 is passed to predict() and reported in both /api/health and per-response meta, but the BOX_DEDUP_IOU comment (lines 123-125) states YOLO26 is NMS-free and the iou= arg is silently ignored — the dedup that actually does this job is BOX_DEDUP_IOU, which is NOT reported anywhere.
confirmed.evidence: Line 632 `iou=YOLO_IOU` (no-op per the project's own finding), lines 1021/1080 report `"yoloIou": YOLO_IOU`. Meanwhile the knob that really governs duplicate suppression, BOX_DEDUP_IOU (line 126), and the fusion knobs (ALPHA_PLASTIC_VOTE/MODE, CONTEXT_PRIOR_MODE, UNSURE_ZOOM, DENSE_RETRY_*) are absent from /api/health. Consequence: health advertises a dead parameter and omits the live ones; a reader tuning WASTEWISE_BOX_DEDUP_IOU can't confirm the deployed value from the API.
confirmed.verdict_note: Confirmed by direct code read. server.py:632 passes iou=YOLO_IOU to predict() while the project's own dated comment (lines 123-125) documents that YOLO26's end-to-end NMS-free predict silently ignores iou=, and the deployed weights are YOLO26m (line 31) so no code path makes YOLO_IOU live. The knob that actually performs duplicate suppression, BOX_DEDUP_IOU (line 126, env-tunable, used at lines 746-774), is absent from both /api/health (lines 1071-1087) and per-response meta (lines 1015-1039), while both report the dead "yoloIou": 0.55 (lines 1021, 1080). Concrete wrong behavior: an operator who sets WASTEWISE_BOX_DEDUP_IOU and checks /api/health cannot confirm the deployed value and instead sees a parameter that does nothing. The fusion knobs (ALPHA_PLASTIC_VOTE/MODE, CONTEXT_PRIOR_MODE, UNSURE_ZOOM*, DENSE_RETRY_*) are likewise unreported. This is stale diagnostic reporting only — inference behavior is unaffected — so the given low severity is correct.

confirmed.title: Stale 2026-07-26 audit comment: zoom retry 'averaged in' vs actual keep-less-Background replacement
confirmed.claim: The dated audit block says the unsure-crop zoom view is 'averaged in', but the implementation replaces the probs wholesale when the zoomed view has lower Background probability — the inline comment at line 738-740 even explains why averaging was abandoned, contradicting the header comment above it.
confirmed.evidence: Line 107-108: 'a 22%-per-side center-shrunk view is averaged in.' Code at lines 736-740: `if float(zoom_probs[j][bg_idx]) < float(verified_probs[i][bg_idx]): verified_probs[i] = zoom_probs[j]` — a conditional replacement, never an average. Someone reproducing the 2026-07-26 sweep from the header comment implements a different (rejected) fusion rule.
confirmed.verdict_note: Confirmed as a stale comment. C:/FYP/web/server.py line 107 says the unsure-crop zoom view "is averaged in", but the implementation (lines 736-740) never averages: it conditionally REPLACES the crop's probs with the zoomed view's probs only when the zoomed view has lower Background probability (`if float(zoom_probs[j][bg_idx]) < float(verified_probs[i][bg_idx]): verified_probs[i] = zoom_probs[j]`), and the inline comment at 737-738 explicitly says averaging was rejected because "averaging instead lets the emptier view's Background veto real objects". The audit trail corroborates the supersession: runs/audits/realworld_fusion_sweep_2026-07-26.json line 1697 records "zoom retry with AVERAGING combine - superseded by v9 pick-view". So the header block describes the v8 (rejected) fusion rule while the code ships v9 pick-view. No runtime misbehavior — this is documentation-only train-of-record skew: anyone reproducing the deployed config from the header comment alone would implement the rejected averaging rule. Severity low is correct (comment fix: change "is averaged in" to "replaces the crop's probs when it shows less Background").

confirmed.title: MIN_RELIABLE_CONF comment claims it gates the headline material vote; it only gates the mixed-load hint
confirmed.claim: The constant's comment says it is the bar 'for counting a box as a reliable material vote (headline material and the mixed-load bin hint)', but the headline-material aggregation counts every non-Background box unconditionally; MIN_RELIABLE_CONF is only consulted in the mixed-bins loop.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 82-84 (comment) vs lines 898-902: `if label_key != "Background": material_counts[...] += 1; material_weights[...] += area_weight * max(0.10, label_conf)` — no confidence bar; the only use is line 978 (mixed_bins). A low-confidence 5% box still votes on dominant_material/bin route (down-weighted, but counted), contrary to the documented contract. Also relevant since 'No waste gate any more' (line 895) — the comment predates that removal.
confirmed.verdict_note: Confirmed by direct inspection of C:/FYP/web/server.py. MIN_RELIABLE_CONF appears exactly four times: the definition + comment (lines 82-84), the accurate mixed-bins comment (line 974), the single functional use in the mixed-bins loop (line 978: `item["confidence"] < int(MIN_RELIABLE_CONF * 100)`), and a metadata echo in the health/info endpoint (line 1085). The headline-material aggregation (lines 898-902) counts every non-Background box unconditionally — `material_counts[...] += 1` and `material_weights[...] += area_weight * max(0.10, label_conf)` — with no confidence bar, and neither the dominant_material selection (line 949) nor its override logic (lines 950-956) consults the constant. So the definition comment's claim that it is the bar for "headline material and the mixed-load bin hint" is half wrong: it gates only the bin hint. This is not a documented measured decision being misread — the dated 2026-07-18 comment at lines 894-897 ("Every non-Background box is a material vote... No waste gate any more") shows the unconditional voting is intentional, which means the constant's comment is simply stale from before that removal, exactly as the finding says. It is a comment/documentation defect only; runtime behavior is intentional and consistent with the mixed-bins comment at lines 969-975. Severity 'low' is correct.

confirmed.title: SAND_SAT_MIN env knob is dead on the deployed Space; ORGANIC_PRIOR_FLOOR silently no-ops with prior mode off
confirmed.claim: WASTEWISE_SAND_SAT_MIN only affects infer_context_hsv (line 467), which is reached solely when the Places365 files are missing — and deploy_hf_space.py unconditionally ships all three Places365 files, so on the production Space the knob is unreachable.
confirmed.evidence: get_scene_net (lines 389-394) falls back to HSV only if weights/cats/IO files are absent; C:/FYP/scripts/deploy_hf_space.py MODEL_FILES (lines 21-23) always includes resnet18_places365.pth.tar, categories_places365.txt, IO_places365.txt. The 2026-07-26 audit comment (line 108) already recorded sand-sat>=50 as rejected; keeping a dead env knob invites someone to set it and observe nothing. Related: ORGANIC_PRIOR_FLOOR IS wired (lines 859-862), but with CONTEXT_PRIOR_MODE=off the prior is uniform 1/6, so any floor <= 0.1667 is a silent no-op — a user setting e.g. 0.10 expecting an organic boost gets nothing, with no indication why.
confirmed.verdict_note: Both sub-claims verified by code trace. (1) SAND_SAT_MIN (web/server.py:115) is used only in infer_context_hsv (line 467), whose sole caller infer_context (line 416) takes the HSV path only when get_scene_net() returns None, i.e. when one of the three Places365 files is absent (lines 389-394; a load exception raises rather than falling back). scripts/deploy_hf_space.py MODEL_FILES (lines 21-23) unconditionally ships all three files, so on the production Space the knob is unreachable — setting WASTEWISE_SAND_SAT_MIN there provably changes nothing. (2) With CONTEXT_PRIOR_MODE=off (the default; the Space Dockerfile sets no override), line 856 uses the uniform default prior [1/6]*6, so the ORGANIC_PRIOR_FLOOR max() at line 861 is an identity for any floor <= 0.1667 — a silent no-op with no warning. The 2026-07-26 audit comment (lines 108-109) documents rejecting the parameter CHANGES (sand-sat>=50, organic floor) by measurement, but that does not make the leftover inert knobs an intended design; they are dead/inert configuration surface that misleads tuning attempts. No wrong predictions arise from defaults, so severity low is correct — the harm is a misleading env-knob surface, fixable by deletion or a startup log.

Suggested fix if desired: have deploy_hf_space.py import LOCALIZER_LABEL from web/server.py (already copied into the deploy dir) when generating the README, and update the stale server.py line 5 docstring.

refuted.title: Alpha blend mixes a non-distribution YOLO vote; net effect is a fixed (1-alpha) Background discount independent of detector score
refuted.why: The arithmetic in the finding is correct (final Background = (1-alpha)*crop_bg; verified the 0.31-conf flip example numerically), but every claimed consequence is coherent, intended-shaped, and measured behavior rather than a defect. (1) yolo_probs[6]=0 is not missing mass — a detector box IS the detector's opinion that the location is not Background, so bg = alpha*0 + (1-alpha)*crop_bg is a standard linear opinion pool; the sub-unit material mass is explicitly handled by the renormalize-then-rescale at server.py:867-875, yielding a proper distribution where material shares still scale with yolo_score. (2) The discount is NOT score-independent: alpha steps 0.15 -> 0.40 at yolo_score 0.30 = YOLO_GATE_CONF, the documented confident-waste threshold; flat-within-branch is how the entire documented "Dynamic Alpha Blending" scheme works. (3) The flip case involves a box above the gate where the detector's measured field precision is ~0.83, so overriding a borderline crop Background 0.55 is not demonstrably wrong. (4) The yolo_key=None path (trash/waste/garbage -> None) still suppressing Background is semantically right (object of unknown material) and is effectively unreachable with the deployed 6-class material detector whose labels all map. (5) The exact deployed mechanism, including both alpha branches and the plastic discount, was swept end-to-end (yolo26s/yolo26m conf_gate_alpha sweeps, realworld_fusion_sweep_2026-07-26 with 8 fusion variants) — the finding itself concedes this. No concrete input/state producing wrong output was traced; the residual issue is that the Background side-effect of alpha deserves a comment, which is a documentation nit, not a medium-severity logic error.

refuted.title: No decoded-size cap: 15MB upload limit does not bound decode memory (decompression bomb / OOM DoS)
refuted.why: The finding's premise ("no pixel-count cap") is factually wrong: OpenCV enforces OPENCV_IO_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS (default 2^30 ~= 1.07 gigapixels) inside cv2.imdecode itself. Verified empirically on the shipped version family (opencv-python-headless>=4.9; tested 4.10.0): the finding's 65500x65500 example raises cv2.error at header-parse time with zero pixel allocation, is caught by the blanket handler at server.py:1123, and returns a 500. Worst reachable decode is capped at 2^30 px x 3B = 3.22GB; a real 625MP JPEG (9.8MB compressed, under the 15MB limit) decodes to 1.9GB in 3.6s. Decode runs inside _inference_lock (server.py:1118) so only one oversized decode can exist at a time, and crops (server.py:669) are numpy views, not copies. The HF Space uses default free hardware (16GB RAM; no suggested_hardware in deploy_hf_space.py), so a bounded 3.2GB transient plus loaded models cannot OOM the container. The residual effect — a crafted image holds the serialized inference lock a few seconds longer than a legitimate 15MB photo — adds no meaningful DoS capability to an already-serialized public demo endpoint. The claimed wrong behavior (unbounded allocation, OOM, container kill) does not occur with any input.

refuted.title: Places365 scene net preprocessing deviates from canonical eval transform (no Resize(256)+CenterCrop(224))
refuted.why: The code fact is accurate (direct 224x224 resize, no CenterCrop) but the defect claim collapses on inspection. (1) The canonical Places365 eval transform is trn.Resize((256,256)) — a tuple — which is itself an anisotropic squash to square; the "aspect-distorting resize vs the reference" contrast is factually wrong. The only real geometric delta is the missing CenterCrop, i.e. this code retains the 12.5% border the reference discards — a marginal perturbation for a whole-scene classifier, not an off-distribution input. (2) Impact is already mitigated by documented design: CONTEXT_PRIOR_MODE defaults to "off" (server.py:122) and line 855-856 forces the fusion prior to "default", so the scene label is a cosmetic UI string with zero effect on class scores, exactly as the dated comment at lines 357-360 states. (3) The exclude_boxes aside is intended: the CNN replaces the HSV heuristic whose failure mode (litter pixels dominating color histograms) is what box-masking existed to fix; the parameter remains for the HSV fallback path at line 416. No concrete input can be traced to a wrong classification or even a demonstrably wrong scene label relative to the reference pipeline.

refuted.title: Keras fallback path is unrunnable on the HF Space: requirements-space.txt ships no TensorFlow
refuted.why: The individual facts are accurate (no TF in requirements-space.txt, .h5 not in MODEL_FILES, Keras import precedes the exists() check in get_models), but the failure state is unreachable through the shipped pipeline. Both tuned files (best_convnext_ensemble_tuned.pth and handcrafted_scaler.npz) are in MODEL_FILES, and copy_tree_item/shutil.copy2 raises at deploy time if either is missing locally — the deploy fails fast before upload. upload_folder is a single atomic commit (LFS pre-upload + one commit), so a "partial upload" cannot leave server.py present but the tuned pair absent on the Space. The Dockerfile COPYs the whole deploy dir and server.py's ROOT resolves to it, so paths line up. The only way into the Keras branch on the Space is a future source edit (dropping/renaming the checkpoint in MODEL_FILES), which is a hypothetical future misconfiguration, not a defect in current code; the Keras branch itself is live, functioning local-dev fallback, not a bug. At most this is a nice-to-have fail-fast guard for API_ONLY mode, not a traceable wrong behavior.
